styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: The Hermitage, the Russian Museum and the Mariinsky.

styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Peter and Paul Fortress, the siege story and the canals.

styles.label: Art
styles.blurb: World-class collections, from icons to the avant-garde.

stays.why: Walk to the Hermitage, Kazan Cathedral and the main metro lines. Noisiest and busiest area.
Quiet streets, the Kunstkamera and the Spit views. Two metro stops from the centre.
Green, local and cheaper. Close to the Peter and Paul Fortress and the zoo.
Calm historic streets near St Isaac's and the Mariinsky Theatre. Good for walkers.

food: Try borscht, pelmeni and blini; lunch deals (business lunch) are much cheaper than dinner, often RUB400–800.
Pyshechnaya on Bolshaya Konyushennaya: cheap hot doughnuts and coffee, a local institution.
Book the famous restaurants ahead; walk-in queues are long on weekends.
Georgian and Uzbek food is popular and good value: khachapuri and plov, about RUB600–1200 a main.
Tipping is not required but 5–10% is welcome. Check if service is already added.
more_time: Add a half-day to Peterhof by hydrofoil from the centre; check sailings and palace closures on the day.
Swap one museum for a canal boat ride: about 1 hour, best in the long evening light of June–July.
Take a day trip to Pushkin (Tsarskoye Selo) for the Catherine Palace; go early to beat the queues.

recommend.why: Three nights covers the Hermitage, the fortress and a canal ride without rushing; add a night for Peterhof.

month_notes: January: highs near -3°C, lows -8°C. Bundle up; museums are warm and quiet.
February: still cold, -2°C to -7°C. Short days; plan indoor sights.
March: around 2°C by day, -4°C at night. Snow turns to slush; wear waterproof boots.
April: 8°C days, 0°C nights. Bridges and parks start to open up.
May: 15°C days, 6°C nights. White nights begin; long evenings for walks.
June: 20°C days, 13°C nights. White Nights peak; book hotels early.
July: warmest, 22°C high, 15°C low. Busiest month; expect 16 rain days.
August: 21°C high, 14°C low. Still warm and busy; carry a light rain jacket.
September: 16°C days, 10°C nights. Fewer crowds, good light for photos.
October: 8°C days, 4°C nights. Wet and grey; pack layers and an umbrella.
November: 3°C days, -1°C nights. Dark and damp; museums are the plan.
December: -1°C high, -4°C low. Cold and festive; short daylight hours.

climate_guide.summary: Humid continental climate: cold winters, mild summers and frequent rain year-round.

items.title: Best time: May to September
items.text: Days of 15–22°C and long evenings. June and July bring the White Nights.

items.title: Cold winters (December to February)
items.text: Highs near -3°C to -1°C and lows to -8°C. Snow and ice on pavements; wear warm boots.

items.title: Rain in every month
items.text: 10–16 rain days a month. July is wettest. Always carry a small umbrella.

items.title: Very short winter days
items.text: December daylight is brief; plan indoor sights and start early.

items.title: Bridge drawbridges
items.text: Bridges rise at night from spring to autumn. Check the schedule before late trips.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Layers, a waterproof jacket and comfortable shoes; a warm coat, hat and gloves in winter.

transit.best: Metro for most trips; walk in the centre and use Yandex Go at night.

modes.text: Fast and cheap: about RUB60 per entry with a Podorozhnik card, about RUB86 by contactless card or token. Runs roughly 05:45 to 00:15; stations are deep, so allow 1-2 min on escalators.
Buses, trolleybuses and trams cover the city; pay by Podorozhnik card or contactless.
Yandex Go (Yandex.Taxi) is the main ride app; local taxi firms also operate.
Not needed in the centre; traffic and parking are hard. Use metro and taxis.
Central sights are walkable; bikes are limited and winter cycling is hard.
Hydrofoils run to Peterhof in season; check sailings on the day.
